previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with atypical chest pain radiating to the neck, arm, and back, following a recent hospitalization for similar symptoms. He had stopped cardiac medications previously, raising concern for stent thrombosis, but serial troponins were negative and a stress test showed no new blockages. Initial fevers and leukocytosis resolved without evidence of infection. He developed opiate withdrawal symptoms during admission, which were managed with clonidine and diazepam. His symptoms improved, and he expressed motivation to remain abstinent from opioids. He was discharged home with continued cardiac medications, referrals for addiction support, and follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ w/ CAD s/p stenting to RCA, LCx, LAD w/ recent MI 
in ___ with several fixed perfusion defect, a history of 
chronic chest pain, anxiety and multiple social issues who 
presents with chest pain.
.
AMA:  The patient left the hospital against medical advice 
stating that his brother had just overdosed and his sister was 
on her way to pick him up.  He was advised to stay until his 
second set of cardiac biomarkers returned and until his heart 
disease could be medically optomized, but left anyways.  He did 
not recieve his cardiac medications prior to leaving AMA, but he 
noted that he would contact his PCP so that they could be phoned 
in to his pharmacy. 
.  
CHEST PAIN/CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE: Patient has an extensive 
cardiac history that was worked up in the previous months with a 
cardiac stress test. Given his intermittent homelessness and 
poor followup he was not considered a candidate for stenting at 
that time. His presenting chest pain was initially concerning 
for cardiac ischemia, but EKG changes were unchanged from prior 
and initial biomarkers were negative, also not relieved by 
nitroglycerin.  Ischemia was felt to be of low concern and 
patient left against medical advice before second set of 
biomarkers returned, but were negative.  We were unable to give 
patient his beta-blocker, ace inhibitor, asprin, plavix or 
statin prior to leaving against medical advice.
.  
SYNCOPAL EVENT: Syncopal event likely in the setting of acute 
alcohol intoxication as cardiac workup was negative. 
.  
POLYSUBSTANCE ABUSE: Spoke with patient's PCP who felt that many 
of the patient's reccent admissions had been secondary to drug 
seeking behavior.  Patient did recieve morphine the setting of 
possible acute coronary syndrome.  But did not recieve anyother 
narcotics.  Was intoxicated at the time of presentation and was 
placed on CIWA prior to leaving AMA.
.  
ANXIETY:  very active, likely lead to patient leaving AMA.  
Unable to treat or optomize prior to leaving.
.
TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
-Cardiac biomarkers negative x2
-needs follow up with PCP for optimal medical management of his 
CAD.
-Needs follow up for drug and alcohol treatment if willing.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ man with syncope, head trauma and on "blood thinners"
(sic).  Assess for traumatic injury.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior studies with the latest CT head on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast MDCT images were acquired through the head. 
Multiplanar reformatted images were obtained for evaluation.

FINDINGS:  There is a moderate subgaleal hematoma in the right parietovertex
scalp with no underlying fracture. There is no acute intracranial hemorrhage,
edema, mass effect or major vascular territorial infarct.  The ventricles and
sulci are normal in size and symmetric in configuration.  There is no shift of
normally midline structures. The gray-white matter differentiation is
well-preserved.  There is no acute fracture.  The visualized paranasal sinuses
are clear.  Left mastoid air cells demonstrate tiny amount of fluid.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Moderate-sized right parietovertex scalp subgaleal hematoma, without skull
fracture.
2.  No acute intracranial injury.  No intracranial hemorrhage.

HISTORY:  ___ man, with syncope, head trauma and on blood thinners. 
Assess for cervical injury.

COMPARISON:  Cervical radiograph on ___ and also CT neck with
contrast on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast MDCT images were acquired from the skull base to the
cervicothoracic junction.  Multiplanar reformatted images were obtained for
evaluation.

FINDINGS:  The study is significantly limited by patient motion, despite
repeat acquisition, with the overall appearance unchanged from the prior CT
neck on ___. 

There is no acute cervical fracture or malalignment.  The prevertebral soft
tissues are normal.  Again noted are significant degenerative changes at
levels C5, C6 and C7 with large anterior osteophytes and left-sided
uncovertebral and facet arthropathy, and severe neural foraminal narrowing at
these levels. There is also a partially calcified C2-3 intervertebral disc. 
The visualized lung apices are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute cervical fracture or malalignment.
2.  Unchanged multilevel degenerative disease.

NOTE ADDED IN ATTENDING REVIEW: There is significant narrowing of the ventral
spinal canal at the C5-6 and C6-7 levels with apparent effacement of the
thecal sac. If there is clinical concern regarding cord injury (eg. new
myelopathy), consideration should be given to dedicated MR study, if feasible.

HISTORY:  ___ man, with chest pain and syncope.  Assess for
pneumothorax or rib fracture.

COMPARISONS:  Multiple prior chest radiographs, with the latest on ___.

AP AND LATERAL CHEST RADIOGRAPHS:  The lungs are fully expanded AND CLEAR.
ONCE AGAIN PULMONARY VASCULATURE IS MILDLY ENGORGED, AS IT WAS ON ___, BUT NOT MOST RECENTLY ON ___. THERE IS NO pneumothorax OR
pleural effusions. The cardiomediastinal silhouette, hilar contours, and

displaced fracture.

IMPRESSION: VASCULAR CONGESTION MAY HERALD CHF.  No radiographic evidence of
acute intrathoracic injury.  No PLEURAL ABNORMALITY or displaced rib fracture.
